triage.title: Box-art retries and saving
triage.label: Backend integration
triage.finding_and_proposed_resolution: Preserve Hollycast physical/online workers, custom source handling and database generations. Adapt backoff/no-progress/save rules to that architecture; this is not a naming fix.
triage.status: analysis only; not implemented or newly approved

preserve: 40-item physical batches with four workers; 10-item online batches
physical-only/custom-first/scraped cover selection and cached fallback
custom indexing, database generation and atomic save protection
separate arcade artwork source; TheGamesDB blackout must stay provider-specific
adaptations: Put the 10-second no-progress gate on online scheduling after local/physical work is allowed to start. Reuse the existing queue and threading model.
Track progress for this scrape batch, not the global databaseDirty flag, which can be set by other Hollycast activity. A completed lookup, even with no matching image, counts as completed work.

Hollycast TheGamesDb::scrape(vector&) catches individual lookup errors internally. Inspect each item completion flag and requeue unfinished items rather than relying only on the outer exception handler; save completed items from a partially successful batch.

Keep markDatabaseDirty/saveDatabase generation checks; saveDatabase already skips a clean database. Avoid declaring no-op/error-only batches dirty instead of replacing Hollycast save logic with Flycast older single-worker code.
Import upstream HTTP 403/429 24-hour blackout and status-bearing warning messages. Keep it in TheGamesDb; the independent arcade source must not acquire a one-day blackout.
user_effects: Successful online scraping gains no fixed per-game delay.
After no-progress work, the online queue waits 10 seconds before another attempt; newly queued online work may share that short wait. Local/custom processing remains available.
TheGamesDB 403 changes from 60 seconds to 24 hours; 429 changes from the generic 1 second to 24 hours. These are the exact upstream timings.
Existing/cached/custom/physical artwork stays visible while missing TheGamesDB artwork waits; arcade source is not subject to the TheGamesDB one-day timer.
Fewer redundant database writes and fewer repeated error-only scrape attempts; failed items remain retryable and successful partial results are retained.
The timer is in scraper memory, not persisted into the artwork database; a full application restart resets that object state.
No new menu setting or popup is included. Failure/status detail is logged.
boxart_adaptation_review.recommendation: Keep upstream 10-second and 24-hour policy unchanged; adapt only the Hollycast worker, completion/retry, and database bookkeeping seams.
boxart_adaptation_review.correction: Earlier summaries saying all failed items naturally reach the outer catch were incomplete: Hollycast catches some errors inside TheGamesDb and the adaptation must account for that.
